dossier.public_summary: The 13-day dip is seen in only four transits, three clustered near the same gap, and one TESS sector shows no dip at all. The host is an active M dwarf that varies more than the dip depth, and close neighbours can still reproduce the signal with a normal stellar eclipse while centroid imaging gives no on-target location. Together this favours spot or blended binary noise over a 3.7 Earth-radius planet.
